key_insight: The quantum switch offers provable query advantages over definite-order circuits: exact worst-case simulation of general channels needs infinitely many calls, while fixed-error approximation can require exponentially many in the qubit count.
engineering_relevance: Quantum-switch-based noise characterization can distinguish noise models with identical entanglement and average gate fidelities, a task relevant to quantum error correction.
method: Analyze black-box query costs for definite-order circuits with classical feed-forward and unlimited ancillary quantum memory.
Prove simulation lower bounds for general channels on d-dimensional systems.
Compare switch and circuit query costs for distinguishing unknown-basis dephasing from depolarizing noise.
evidence_signal: Theoretical bounds show Ω(d^{1/4}) calls for simulation below 1/2 half-diamond-norm error and Ω(d^{1/16}) calls for noise discrimination, versus dimension-independent switch use at fixed noise strength.
watch_item: These are theoretical query advantages; practical gains depend on implementing the quantum switch reliably and accounting for experimental overhead.
paper_title: Infinite or indefinite: the query cost of simulating the quantum switch
